messages:
maria: Heads-up — nightly evals flagged a regression after v9 bring-up. Quality metric (conv_prompt_pass) down ~3.2% vs v8. Failing cases cluster on non-ASCII prompts (es/fr/zh). Possible tokenizer offset changes + post-quantization smearing. sample below.

aj: Ugh. Can you paste a minimal repro and the eval link?

maria: Eval dashboard: https://redwood/evals/nightly/2026-03-19/v9

maria: Minimal repro (spanish):
```
PROMPT: "Resume esto en 2 frases: ¿Cuál es el objetivo principal del ensayo?"
MODEL=v9-quant
GENERATION: "El objetivo principal del ensayo es..."
TOKEN_OFFSETS: [0, 6, 12, 16, 22, 28]  <-- looks shifted vs v8
EXPECTED_ALIGNMENT: token 3 should map to "del" but maps to "del " (non-breaking?)
```

sam: Interesting — offset shift could break span extraction/evals that check exact substrings. Any tokenizer diffs in the commit?

maria: v9 commit: a1b2c3d4. Tokenizer bump included: support for multilingual normalization (NFKC tweak) + added nonascii-preservation flag. Not sure which line introduced this.

leo: Could be the normalizer changes. NFKC will normalize some composed characters -> lengths change. But "smearing" after quant could also change generation boundaries. Do we have an unquantized v9 run?

maria: Yes — v9-fp16 (unquant) shows smaller but present shift (~0.9% fail). v9-quant shows the worst (3.2%). So two factors: tokenizer baseline shift + quant amplifies generation differences.

aj: Can we bisect tokenizer vs weights? Quick plan: run v8-weights + v9-tokenizer, and v9-weights + v8-tokenizer, with the same eval seed set. If v8w+v9tok fails -> tokenizer; else weights. @sam can you kick off?

sam: On it. Starting two eval runs now: `pytest evals/nightly/test_suite.py::conv_prompt_set -k multilingual --model-overrides "weights:v8,tokenizer:v9"` and the reverse. Will post results.

ci-bot: nightly-evals job #4821 started for tag v9 (jobs: multilingual-compat-check). Logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/4821

nina: Also flag: reranker/eval that does token-span scoring uses exact .find() on the generated text. If offsets shift by a single codepoint, scoring breaks. We should switch that eval to normalized matching (NFKC-aware) as a short-term.

leo: Agreed. Add a tolerant comparator: normalize both prompt and generation before index matching. But that is a bandaid — we need to decide whether to keep tokenizer change. Are there security/regression reasons the NFKC change was needed?

maria: The tokenizer change fixed several tokenization regressions for Indic scripts and reduced OOV rate in some benchmarks. So it had net wins for coverage. But the offset change is problematic for downstream substring-based tooling.

aj: If we keep tokenizer change, we must: (1) update eval scoring to NFKC-normalized matching, (2) update docs for tokenizer break, (3) add conversion utility to map old offsets -> new offsets for customers migrating.

sam: Update: v8w+v9tok run shows failrate 2.9% (same as v9 overall). v9w+v8tok run shows failrate 0.5% (near v8 baseline). So root cause = tokenizer change.

maria: Thanks. Will open a mitigation PR: pin tokenizer to v8 for hosted until we finish migration + add normalized matching in evals. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/ops/patch/2345

aj: Can you add a small compatibility note in release notes and email infra + docs? Also add a runtime flag for private deployments to opt into the new tokenizer so customers can test before force-upgrading.

nina: I'll draft the eval comparator change: function tolerant_find(hay, needle) { return normalize(hay) .indexOf(normalize(needle)); } and a few unit tests.

maria: Action items: 1) revert tokenizer in hosted (maria) 2) add normalized comparator (nina) 3) add release note + migration guide (aj) 4) run targeted multilingual evals post-change (sam). I'll update thread when PRs land. :thumbsup:

leo: One more note — for the quant path, let's run a small quant-sensitivity test after we stabilize tokenizer: `python tools/quant_sweep.py --model v9 --seeds 10 --metric conv_prompt_pass` to confirm quant doesn't amplify other tiny diffs.

maria: Good call. I'll queue it after revert. Thanks all.

sam: CI job #4821 finished: v8w+v9tok logs here: https://ci.redwood/jobs/4821/logs — attaching sample diff.

maria: Received. Put pinned rollback and the eval comparator PR in review. Will follow up with migration timeline.
